title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve fleet burst controls and utilization reporting
author: Maya Patel
description: This PR adds smoother burst-control behavior to the dedicated fleet autoscaler and improves utilization reporting used by the Console and billing. Motivation: customers observed spiky burst usage causing rapid scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs which increased cost and thrash. Additionally, fleet-level utilization and per-pool token-bucket reporting was noisy and did not expose short-term burst headroom. Changes include: 1) Token-bucket smoothing: introduce a configurable smoothing window (default 60s) when computing available burst tokens to avoid reacting to transient traffic spikes. 2) Backpressure + graceful shed: add a soft-backpressure stage that denies lower-priority requests when burst headroom is exhausted instead of immediately dropping all new requests. 3) Throughput guarantees: add per-pool guaranteed throughput config with clear fallback to best-effort when capacity constrained. 4) Utilization reporting: export new metrics (dedicated_pool_burst_headroom_seconds, dedicated_pool_utilization_percent, dedicated_pool_sustained_tokens_used) and add aggregated time-windowed stats (1m/5m/1h) to the Console UI. 5) Telemetry and alerting: emit events when pools enter sustained-burst mode so SRE can create alerts. 6) Compatibility: rollout is opt-in via autoscaler.policy.v2 flag to preserve existing behavior; migration guide included in docs. The description below contains implementation details, testing plan, and rollout checklist. Implementation details: token-bucket smoothing is implemented in autoscaler/tokenbucket/smoother.go and tuned via AutoscalerPolicy.SmoothingWindowSeconds. Backpressure is implemented as a priority gate in autoscaler/queue/priority_gate.go that consults pool priority maps. Metrics are added to telemetry/metrics_registry.go and exposed via /metrics and the Console aggregation endpoint. API changes: new optional fields under DedicatedAutoscalerPolicy: smoothing_window_seconds, guaranteed_throughput_rps, backpressure_policy. Testing: unit tests added under autoscaler/*_test.go, integration test simulating spike workloads in perf-canary harness, and E2E in redwood-quickstarts that exercises the Console dashboards. Rollout plan: behind feature flag; staged rollout to canary fleet, then 10%/50%/100% with metrics monitoring. See linked Linear tickets for follow-up work.
